chapter: Pope family and the Excelsior Band
title: Taking over the band; instrumentation and saxophones
summary: Pope led the band c.1908 for 28 years; fourteen pieces, trumpets, altos, trombones, two drummers; saxophones only in the 1920s.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone

blocks.x: No. And I'm saying now, back in his days, they practically done almost the same way that we've done during my career. Which I'd taken over, oh, I should say around about 19-8.
And I carried on for about 28 years. And did you say that you played the cornet? I played the trumpet. The trumpet. And your father played the cornet or trumpet? The cornet.
He played E-flat. E-flat. And I started going to the cornet that you have there. Yes. Short the cornet like that. Yes. Yes.
Yes. Was the latter days why. Did you have three cornet players in the band, three trumpet players?
We had around four at all times. Four. Four. How many were in the excel of your band? Fourteen.
Fourteen. And there was four trumpet, three alto players, you know the old time altos. Yes. And two trombone, baritone, bass, two drummers.
Once in a while we'd pick up a paramedic player, another summer. But not all the time? No, not all the time.
Did they have any saxophones in those days? No. Well, yes they did. But we didn't use them. In the latter days we did. When did you start to use the saxophone?
